task_instance: Follow the skill's exact discovery procedure to determine the active AWS profile, region, account ID, and caller ARN in this runtime, using `aws configure list` and `aws sts get-caller-identity` as the skill prescribes, then classify the caller principal per the skill's ARN table.
blocker_detail: The runtime has the AWS CLI installed (aws-cli/1.46.1) and a ~/.aws/config file with only a [default] profile (no region field, no named profiles to check). No AWS_PROFILE/AWS_REGION/AWS_DEFAULT_REGION env vars are set, so per the skill's own resolution order, region resolution fails at all four automatic steps (would have to ask the user, who cannot answer in this session). More fundamentally, `aws configure list` shows access_key/secret_key are present only as masked env-sourced values with no region, and running `aws sts get-caller-identity` (the skill's core command, needed to confirm credentials and obtain the Account ID and Arn) fails with 'InvalidClientTokenId: The security token included in the request is invalid.' There is no ~/.aws/credentials file and no working AWS account behind this sandbox's aws CLI. The skill's core deliverable -- discovering a *real* account id, region, and caller identity -- cannot be produced without valid AWS credentials tied to an actual AWS account, which this runtime does not provide (and obtaining one would require an account-bound/paid AWS service, which the safety rules forbid pursuing).
tools_used: Bash (aws --version, aws configure list, aws sts get-caller-identity, cat ~/.aws/config)
evidence:
Commands run in /tmp/.../exec_ext/huggingface__skills__hf-cloud-aws-context-discovery:
$ aws --version -> aws-cli/1.46.1 Python/3.11.15
$ echo $AWS_PROFILE / $AWS_REGION / $AWS_DEFAULT_REGION -> all empty
$ cat ~/.aws/config -> '[default]\ns3 =\n  payload_signing_enabled = false' (no region field, no other profiles, no credentials file present)
$ aws configure list -> profile <not set>; access_key/secret_key shown as masked 'env' values; region <not set>
$ aws sts get-caller-identity -> 'An error occurred (InvalidClientTokenId) when calling the GetCallerIdentity operation: The security token included in the request is invalid.'
This reproduces exactly the skill's own stated stop condition ('If something is wrong (credentials expired, profile doesn't exist, no region anywhere), stop and surface the specific error before continuing') -- both the region-resolution chain and the credential validation dead-end, with no path to a real account id/ARN in this sandbox.
